headline: Chrome rolls out new warnings for suspicious and scam websites
summary: Google is adding new Chrome warnings that flag suspicious or dangerous websites, which Bleeping Computer reports also use Gemini AI to detect scams and ClickFix attacks.

claims.statement: Chrome is rolling out new warnings for suspicious or dangerous websites.

sources.quote: Chrome will now show a warning before you visit ‘suspicious’ sites
Google’s browser will flash two types of warnings based on whether the site is deemed dangerous or just suspicious.

claims.statement: The suspicious-site warnings require Chrome's Enhanced Protection setting and build on a two-stage system Chrome introduced for downloads in 2024.

sources.quote: The new suspicious site warnings, available when Chrome's Enhanced Protection is on, build on a similar two-stage system introduced for Chrome file downloads in 2024, which provides

claims.statement: Chrome's new scam protections also use Gemini AI to detect deceptive websites and warn users about ClickFix attacks.

sources.quote: Chrome is getting new scam protections that use Gemini to detect deceptive websites and warn users when they copy suspicious commands from ClickFix attacks.

discrepancies.explanation: Bleeping Computer attributes the detection specifically to Gemini AI and highlights ClickFix attacks, details the other outlets' texts do not mention.

quotes.quote: Chrome is getting new scam protections that use Gemini to detect deceptive websites and warn users when they copy suspicious commands from ClickFix attacks.
